question.text: Nisha has agricultural income of Rs.3,00,000 and non-agricultural income of Rs.4,50,000 in FY 2024-25. Under the old tax regime, how is her agricultural income treated for tax purposes?

answer.text: Agricultural income is fully taxable along with non-agricultural income
Agricultural income is exempt but partially integrated with non-agricultural income for rate purposes since non-agricultural income exceeds the basic exemption limit
Agricultural income is fully exempt with no integration required regardless of other income
Agricultural income is exempt only up to Rs.2,50,000 and the balance is taxable

explanation.text: The Logic: Agricultural income is exempt under Section 10(1) of the Income Tax Act. However, the Act applies a partial-integration rule for rate-purpose computation when (a) the taxpayer's non-agricultural income exceeds the basic exemption limit and (b) the agricultural income exceeds Rs.5,000. In that case, agricultural income is not taxed directly, but it is added to non-agricultural income to determine the slab rate at which the non-agricultural income is taxed. For Nisha, non-agricultural income of Rs.4,50,000 exceeds the basic exemption limit, so partial integration applies: her agricultural Rs.3,00,000 stays exempt as income but raises the effective slab on her Rs.4,50,000. The Trap: Making agricultural income fully taxable (Option A) ignores the Section 10(1) exemption. "Fully exempt with no integration" (Option C) is incorrect once non-agricultural income crosses the basic exemption limit — the rate-purpose integration kicks in. The "exempt only up to Rs.2,50,000" answer invents a non-existent ceiling on agricultural-income exemption. Note: The cited NISM Series X-B Investment Adviser Level 2 workbook pages reviewed in the audit confirm that Section 10(1) Agriculture Income is listed as exempt, but the partial-integration mechanics, the Rs.5,000 agriculture threshold, the basic-exemption condition, and the rate-purpose computation are not on the pages checked. The framing above reflects the standard treatment of agricultural income under the Income Tax Act.
